blogPosts.title: How Much Does a New Concrete Driveway Cost in Geelong in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the real cost of a new concrete driveway in Geelong. We break down pricing per square metre, material choices, and what affects your final quote from Wilo's.
body: Planning a new concrete driveway in Geelong? You are not alone. With the city's ongoing residential growth and renewal of older suburbs, driveway upgrades are one of the most common projects local homeowners undertake. The cost of a concrete driveway in Geelong typically ranges from $50 to $120 per square metre for a plain finish, with exposed aggregate and decorative options pushing that figure higher. However, the final price depends on several critical factors including driveway dimensions, soil conditions, access constraints, and the finish you select. In this guide, Wilo's Concreting breaks down real Geelong pricing so you can budget with confidence and avoid nasty surprises when your quote arrives.

The base cost of a concrete driveway in Geelong covers materials, labour, and essential site preparation. Ready-mix concrete is generally priced between $250 and $350 per cubic metre, depending on the mix strength specified for your project. Labour rates in the Geelong region typically run between $50 and $80 per hour for experienced concreters. For a standard single-car driveway measuring approximately 3 metres by 6 metres, you can expect a total cost starting from around $1,500 for a basic broom finish. A double-car driveway at 6 metres by 6 metres will likely start from $3,500 onwards. These figures include excavation, formwork, pouring, finishing, and site clean-up by a professional team.

Driveway thickness is another factor that directly influences both cost and longevity. For standard residential vehicles, Australian Standards recommend a minimum thickness of 100mm for driveways on well-compacted ground. If your Geelong property has reactive clay soils, common in certain pockets around Belmont and Highton, a thicker pour of 125mm or even 150mm may be required along with additional steel reinforcement. Heavier vehicles or commercial driveways may demand 150mm to 200mm reinforced slabs. Each additional 25mm of thickness adds roughly $5 to $10 per square metre to your project cost. Wilo's always conducts thorough site assessments to determine the correct specification for your specific Geelong location.

The finish you choose for your Geelong driveway has a significant impact on the overall cost. A basic broom finish is the most economical option, offering reliable slip resistance at the lowest price point. Exposed aggregate, one of Geelong's most popular driveway finishes, typically adds $15 to $30 per square metre on top of the base cost depending on the aggregate stone selected. Honed concrete, which provides a smooth yet textured surface, sits in a similar price range. Stamped or patterned concrete, replicating the look of natural stone or brick pavers, can add $25 to $50 per square metre. While these premium finishes cost more upfront, they significantly enhance your property's curb appeal and resale value across the competitive Geelong market.

Site preparation is often the most variable cost component for driveway projects in Geelong. If your existing driveway needs demolition and removal, expect to add $20 to $40 per square metre. Geelong's diverse topography means some properties require significant cut and fill work to achieve correct falls for drainage. Soft or waterlogged ground, common near Geelong's waterfront areas, may need additional subgrade stabilisation or gravel base layers. Proper drainage is essential in the Geelong climate, where winter rainfall can be heavy and persistent. A quality concreter will always include adequate falls and drainage solutions in their site preparation scope to prevent water pooling and surface deterioration over time.

Council approval requirements are an important consideration for any driveway project in Geelong. The City of Greater Geelong requires a planning permit for new crossovers or alterations to existing vehicle crossings connecting to the road. This typically costs between $200 and $500 depending on the scope of work. If your driveway is within a heritage overlay area, common in parts of central Geelong, additional approvals may be necessary. Working with an experienced local concreter like Wilo's means these requirements are handled correctly from the start, avoiding costly delays or compliance issues. We ensure all driveway work meets relevant Australian Standards and local council specifications.

When budgeting for your Geelong concrete driveway, the smartest approach is to request detailed written quotes from at least two or three local concreters. A comprehensive quote should itemise excavation, base preparation, concrete supply, reinforcement, pouring, finishing, and clean-up as separate line items. Be wary of quotes that seem significantly lower than others, as they may exclude essential components like proper drainage or adequate thickness. Wilo's Concreting provides transparent, fixed-price quotes for all driveway projects across Geelong, so you know exactly what you are paying before any work begins. Contact us today for a free on-site assessment and obligation-free quote for your new driveway.

blogPosts.title: Best Time to Pour Concrete in Geelong's Coastal Climate
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn when to schedule your concrete pour in Geelong for optimal results. We explain how temperature, humidity, and seasonal conditions affect your project.
body: Timing is everything when it comes to pouring concrete, and in Geelong's unique coastal climate, choosing the right season can make a significant difference to your project's outcome. Geelong experiences a temperate oceanic climate with mild summers, cool winters, and consistent rainfall throughout the year. These conditions present both opportunities and challenges for concrete work. Pouring in the wrong conditions can lead to surface cracking, poor curing, and reduced structural integrity. In this guide, Wilo's Concreting explains the best times to pour concrete in Geelong and how professional concreters adapt their methods to suit the local climate year-round.

Spring and autumn are generally considered the ideal seasons for concrete pouring in Geelong. During these transitional months, temperatures typically sit between 12 and 22 degrees Celsius, providing optimal curing conditions. The moderate humidity levels help prevent the concrete from drying too quickly, which is one of the leading causes of surface cracking. September through November and March through May offer the most predictable weather windows, with lower rainfall averages compared to winter. Wilo's Concreting schedules the majority of our driveway and slab projects during these months, as the stable conditions allow us to achieve the best possible finish and long-term durability for our Geelong clients.

Summer concrete pours in Geelong require careful planning and experienced execution. While the warmer temperatures of December through February can accelerate the curing process, extreme heat above 35 degrees Celsius poses real risks. Hot weather causes surface moisture to evaporate rapidly, leading to plastic shrinkage cracks before the concrete has properly set. Professional concreters in Geelong counter this by scheduling pours for early morning, using curing compounds, and keeping freshly poured concrete moist for the first 48 to 72 hours. If a summer pour is unavoidable for your project, Wilo's employs specialised techniques to protect your concrete from the effects of Geelong's hottest days.

Winter concrete pours in Geelong, from June through August, demand the most careful consideration. While Geelong rarely experiences the harsh freezing conditions seen in inland Victoria, overnight temperatures can drop below 5 degrees Celsius, which significantly slows the hydration process. Concrete poured in cold conditions takes considerably longer to cure and reach its design strength. There is also an increased risk of frost damage if temperatures drop near freezing during the initial curing period. Wilo's Concreting uses insulated blankets, accelerator admixtures, and adjusted mix designs to ensure winter pours in Geelong achieve the same quality and durability as those completed in more favourable conditions.

Geelong's proximity to the coast introduces additional factors that affect concrete curing. The sea breeze can increase surface evaporation rates even on mild days, particularly for exposed slabs and driveways in coastal suburbs like Belmont and Hamlyn Heights. Morning dew and coastal moisture, while beneficial for curing, can also delay finishing operations if the surface is too wet. Rain is perhaps the most disruptive factor, as fresh concrete exposed to rainfall within the first few hours can suffer surface damage and weakened strength. Experienced Geelong concreters like Wilo's monitor weather forecasts closely and adjust their pouring schedules to avoid adverse conditions.

Regardless of the season, proper curing is the most critical factor in achieving durable, long-lasting concrete in Geelong. Curing is the process of maintaining adequate moisture and temperature conditions after pouring, allowing the concrete to gain strength gradually. For Geelong's climate, a minimum curing period of seven days is recommended, with 28 days for full design strength. Methods include wet curing with hessian, applying curing membranes, or using plastic sheeting to retain moisture. Wilo's Concreting ensures every project receives appropriate curing attention, regardless of the season, to deliver concrete that withstands Geelong's coastal environment for decades.

The best approach to timing your Geelong concrete project is to work with an experienced local concreter who understands the regional climate patterns. Wilo's Concreting has poured concrete across Geelong in every season, and we know how to adapt our techniques to achieve excellent results year-round. Whether you need a new driveway, commercial slab, or exposed aggregate patio, we will advise you on the optimal timing for your specific project and location within Geelong. Contact us today to discuss your project timeline and receive a free, no-obligation quote tailored to your needs and the current seasonal conditions.

blogPosts.title: Exposed Aggregate vs Stamped Concrete for Geelong Homes
blogPosts.excerpt: Choosing between exposed aggregate and stamped concrete for your Geelong property? Compare costs, durability, maintenance, and visual appeal to decide.
body: Selecting the right concrete finish is one of the most important decisions Geelong homeowners face when planning a new driveway, patio, or outdoor area. Two of the most popular decorative options are exposed aggregate and stamped concrete, both offering distinct advantages in terms of aesthetics, durability, and value. While both finishes serve the same fundamental purpose of providing a hard-wearing surface, they achieve very different visual results and come with different maintenance requirements. In this comprehensive guide, Wilo's Concreting compares exposed aggregate and stamped concrete specifically for Geelong homes, helping you choose the finish that best suits your property, lifestyle, and budget.

Exposed aggregate concrete is created by pouring a standard concrete slab and then washing away the top layer of cement paste to reveal the decorative stones and pebbles underneath. This finish is enormously popular across Geelong, from new builds in Waurn Ponds to renovations in established suburbs like Geelong West and Highton. The natural stone aggregate provides a textured, slip-resistant surface that handles Geelong's wet winters exceptionally well. With dozens of aggregate options available, from earthy browns and greys to bold reds and blacks, homeowners can create a driveway or patio that complements their home's architecture and the surrounding landscape perfectly.

Stamped concrete, also known as patterned or imprinted concrete, involves pressing moulds into freshly poured concrete to replicate the appearance of natural stone, brick, slate, or tile. The surface is then coloured using integral pigments or surface hardeners to achieve a realistic look. For Geelong homes, stamped concrete offers tremendous visual versatility, allowing you to match the aesthetic of premium paving materials at a fraction of the cost. Popular patterns in the Geelong area include cobblestone, Ashlar slate, and timber plank effects. However, stamped concrete requires precise timing during installation, making the skill and experience of your Geelong concreter absolutely critical to the final result.

When comparing durability, both finishes perform well in Geelong's conditions, but with some important differences. Exposed aggregate is inherently durable because the decorative elements are the actual stones embedded within the concrete itself. This finish handles heavy traffic, resists abrasion, and maintains its appearance with minimal degradation over decades. Stamped concrete, while durable, relies on surface colour and pattern for its visual appeal. Over time, high-traffic areas may show wear to the coloured surface, particularly in Geelong's coastal suburbs where salt air can accelerate surface deterioration. For driveways with regular vehicle traffic, exposed aggregate generally offers superior long-term durability compared to stamped alternatives.

Maintenance requirements differ significantly between the two finishes. Exposed aggregate concrete in Geelong requires relatively low maintenance, with occasional sealing every two to three years to protect against staining and enhance the stone colour. The textured surface naturally hides minor wear and dirt accumulation. Stamped concrete demands more regular maintenance, including resealing every one to two years to protect the coloured surface from UV fading and wear. In Geelong's sunny summers, unsealed stamped concrete can fade noticeably within a few seasons. For busy Geelong families and property investors seeking a low-maintenance option, exposed aggregate consistently proves to be the more practical long-term choice.

Cost is always a key consideration for Geelong homeowners comparing these finishes. Exposed aggregate typically costs between $75 and $130 per square metre installed, depending on the aggregate stone selected and the project size. Stamped concrete generally ranges from $80 to $150 per square metre, with more complex patterns and multiple colours pushing the price higher. While the upfront costs can be comparable, the long-term maintenance costs of stamped concrete often exceed those of exposed aggregate due to more frequent resealing requirements. For Geelong homeowners seeking the best balance of upfront cost, visual appeal, and long-term value, exposed aggregate consistently delivers strong results.

Ultimately, the choice between exposed aggregate and stamped concrete for your Geelong property comes down to your priorities. If you want a naturally beautiful, slip-resistant surface with excellent durability and low maintenance, exposed aggregate is likely your best option. If you prefer the specific look of brick, stone, or slate and are prepared to invest in ongoing maintenance, stamped concrete may be the right choice. Either way, working with an experienced Geelong concreter ensures your chosen finish is installed correctly and performs beautifully for years to come. Wilo's Concreting can show you samples of both finishes and help you make an informed decision for your home.

blogPosts.title: Why Professional Excavation Matters for Your Geelong Construction Project
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover why proper excavation is critical for construction projects in Geelong. Learn about soil types, drainage needs, and the cost of cutting corners.
body: Every successful construction project in Geelong begins underground. Whether you are building a new home extension, installing a concrete slab, or preparing a site for commercial development, professional excavation is the foundation upon which everything else depends. Poor excavation work is one of the leading causes of structural issues, drainage failures, and costly remediation projects across the Geelong region. With the area's diverse soil conditions, varying water tables, and specific council requirements, cutting corners on site preparation is a gamble that rarely pays off. In this guide, Wilo's Concreting explains why professional excavation matters and what Geelong property owners need to know.

Geelong sits on a surprisingly diverse range of soil types that directly impact excavation requirements. The western suburbs, including Belmont and Highton, often feature reactive clay soils that expand and contract significantly with moisture changes. Coastal areas near Geelong's waterfront may have sandy or loose alluvial soils requiring different handling techniques. The newer developments around Waurn Ponds and Armstrong Creek often encounter limestone substrata that demand specialised excavation equipment. Understanding your specific soil conditions is essential for determining the correct excavation depth, base preparation method, and foundation design. Professional excavators like Wilo's conduct thorough site assessments to identify soil conditions before any work begins on your Geelong project.

Drainage is perhaps the most critical consideration during excavation in Geelong's climate. The city receives an average of 500 to 600 millimetres of rainfall annually, with winter months bringing the heaviest precipitation. Without proper drainage planning during the excavation phase, your concrete slab or building foundation is vulnerable to water damage, hydrostatic pressure, and gradual subsidence. Professional excavation involves creating accurate falls and grades that direct water away from structures and into appropriate drainage systems. For slab-on-ground construction, this includes preparing a correctly compacted sub-base with adequate drainage layer thickness. Wilo's integrates comprehensive drainage solutions into every excavation project across the Geelong region.

The equipment used for excavation matters as much as the technique itself. Different project types and soil conditions in Geelong require specific machinery, from mini excavators for tight residential access to larger machines for commercial site preparation. Using the wrong equipment can result in over-excavation, soil disturbance, or damage to adjacent structures and underground services. Geelong's older suburbs, with their narrow access ways and established landscaping, demand particularly careful machine operation and planning. Professional excavation teams maintain a fleet of appropriately sized equipment and hold the operator certifications required for safe, efficient work. Wilo's Concreting operates modern, well-maintained excavation equipment suitable for projects of all sizes across the Geelong region.

Council regulations and utility location are essential components of professional excavation in Geelong. Before any digging commences, all underground services must be located and marked to prevent dangerous and costly strikes. The City of Greater Geelong requires appropriate permits for excavation work that affects road reserves, drainage infrastructure, or boundary areas. Building permits for new construction also typically specify excavation and foundation requirements that must be met before the project can receive a compliance certificate. An experienced Geelong excavator understands these regulatory requirements and ensures full compliance throughout the project. Wilo's manages all necessary permits and service location requests as part of our comprehensive excavation service.

The long-term cost implications of poor excavation cannot be overstated for Geelong property owners. Inadequate site preparation is responsible for a significant percentage of concrete failures across the region, from cracking and settlement to drainage failure and structural movement. Remediation work to fix these issues typically costs three to five times more than doing the excavation properly in the first instance. For Geelong property owners, investing in professional excavation at the outset protects your concrete investment and prevents expensive future repairs. Wilo's Concreting has rectified numerous failed projects across Geelong where initial excavation was inadequate, reinforcing our commitment to getting the foundation right every single time.

When planning your next Geelong construction project, ensure excavation is given the priority and budget it deserves from the very start. Start by engaging a professional team with proven local experience, proper equipment, and comprehensive insurance coverage. Ask detailed questions about their approach to soil assessment, drainage design, and compliance with Australian Standards. Request references from similar projects completed in the Geelong area to verify their track record. Wilo's Concreting brings years of local excavation and concreting experience to every project, combining technical expertise with intimate knowledge of Geelong's unique ground conditions. Contact us today for a thorough site assessment and detailed quote for your excavation or concreting project.
